a.text: I am dreaming.
In the dream, it is the day my mother first brought me to Rhodes Island. She took me, a young child, to the huge landship to meet one person after another.
Their faces are blurry, their voices distant.
I had a feeling that my mother had made an important decision.
I was too young at the time. I naively thought that nothing short of death could separate me from my mother.
Until an adult led me away, while my mother stood there and watched.
I turned around to look at her, but I couldn't discern the emotions in her eyes.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: So, uhh, GreyThroat... Is that what you go by now?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: That's right. And you are?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Umm... Do you really not recognize me?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Sir, you're bringing news of a Catastrophe. Though the situation isn't particularly urgent, I don't think we have time to play guessing games with one another.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Fair enough. After all, it's been so many years, and you were still so young back then.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Here, this is a photo I took with your parents. Does it jog your memory?

In the photo, the man in front of me looks as old as I am now. He stands next to my mother and father with his arms folded. There's a date in the lower right corner, and it's not long after my eighth birthday.
There are a few words written on the back of the photo: 'For Ian Caldwell.'

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Ian Caldwell... My father's student. I remember you. You used to stop by our house often.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Righto. That's me.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You've changed an awful lot.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: So what should I call you? GreyThroat, or...

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: GreyThroat's fine.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Sounds good. Anyway, I'm here for one other thing, besides warning you about the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I'd like you to be my bodyguard.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Leaving Rhodes Island to be... your bodyguard? That's unrealistic.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: And even if you were my father's student, why did it take you so many years to find Rhodes Island and me?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I only ran into you again a few months ago, during the Catastrophe that struck the Winterwisp Mountains in the north of Leithanien.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...In Wolumonde?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Right, the Catastrophe that tore through Wolumonde. Had it not been for you and your team, things could've gone a whole lot worse.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Unfortunately, you were already evacuating when I saw you, and I was rushing to the scene. You looked familiar, but I didn't have time to actually confirm it was you.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: After that, I found out from the Catastrophe Messenger information network that it really was you.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: And what does that have to do with me becoming your bodyguard?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: You weren't this distrustful when you were a kid. Have they been... treating you alright on Rhodes Island all these years?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Your mother... I met her after the incident that took my teacher's life. She was looking everywhere for a place where you would be taken care of.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: And she came to you?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: The other way around. I offered to take care of you and your mother for a while, but she turned me down.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: She did? Why?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Maybe because I could barely support myself at the time.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Your parents treated me well, even letting me stay at your place for a while. So, I've always felt bad about what happened.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Also... I've seen how you interact with the Infected.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: You rescued an Infected somewhere near the Winterwisp Mountains outside of Wolumonde.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Something like that should have been a piece of cake for Rhodes Island, but when you were helping the Infected—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Heyo—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh, are you chatting with a guest?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Just about done. What's up?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Who's this?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Blaze, Rhodes Island elite operator. Blaze, this is Ian, one of my father's students.
Blaze saunters over off-handedly and leans against the wall.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: According to our estimates, a Catastrophe will hit in roughly three to five days. I'll be staying in the area for about a day or two.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: If you've made up your mind, come and see me. I'll be staying in a town slightly north of where Rhodes Island is anchored.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Sorry for interrupting.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You don't seem sorry at all.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh, really?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: C'mon, don't be all stony-faced like that. You're still young, y'know. You won't get wrinkles by having more expressions.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...What on earth brings you here?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: There's a party on the deck tomorrow night. Wanna come?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Oh wow, this is rare. You're actually considering it?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I thought you'd blow me off like usual and say, 'I'm not going anywhere with you.'

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: And each time, you'd come over five minutes before the party started and drag me there anyway.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: See, you get it after all.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Or, are you hesitating... because you've decided to accept Ian's offer?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: For the record, I just happened to overhear your conversation when I came in. Wasn't trying to eavesdrop or anything, sorry.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Because I seem more genuinely sorry this time?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Something like that.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Jokes aside, what do you think about his offer?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: There's no way I'll accept it, but I should at least have a talk with him.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: When is Rhodes Island leaving?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Seeing how the Catastrophe alert puts us at risk in about three to five days, we're probably setting off in the next twenty-four hours.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No worries though, there's enough time. Even if your chat with the dude takes longer than expected, I'll buy you some time by talking the engine guy into having a few drinks in the boiler room.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Glad you decided to come, GreyThroat.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Want something to drink? The townspeople are preparing to evacuate, so everything's cheap right now.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...I'll pass.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Let's circle back to our conversation about my mother. Did she leave anything behind, or... did you learn anything about her during your time as a Messenger?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: ...Unfortunately, no.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I tried looking for her but with no success. That said, I could search more efficiently with you as my bodyguard.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I still don't get it.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I understand why you're looking for a bodyguard. Maybe your old one has resigned or passed away. Whatever the case, you urgently need a new one now.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: But why me? Because of the rescue mission in Wolumonde? Or because you want to help me out and make up for what you couldn't do for me in the past?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: If you insist on putting it that way, then yes, I'd like to help you.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Remember what I never got to finish saying on Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: While you were helping that Infected man back in the Winterwisp Mountains, your hands were shaking the whole time, and your whole body was... emanating terror.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I knew in that instant that... we were exactly the same.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: How so?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Have you never wondered why I'm a Catastrophe Messenger now when I used to be your father's student?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Because I also lost a few of my kin in the unrest that took your father's life...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: From then on, I'll feel nauseous whenever I see those hideous Originium crystals in the flesh beneath my scalpel.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Whenever I think of the Oripathy medicine in the bottles, I can't help but think we'd be better off investing resources in diseases that can be cured, rather than throwing them away at this incurable disease.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: You get along pretty well with that Blaze girl, right? But when she was leaning against the wall, you couldn't control your urge to shift away from her.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...It's just a subconscious reaction.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I can tell, GreyThroat. You've been living an oppressive life all these years on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I hope you can find another place that suits you better. Stop forcing yourself to walk on a path you could have avoided.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I was raised on Rhodes Island, Ian. I'm not enough of an ingrate to cast aside the Infected for such a petty reason.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: You'll still be helping them, just in a different way.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Helping people avoid Catastrophes by nipping the very source of infection in the bud. How is that not helping them?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Sure, they might have raised you, but that doesn't mean you need to heed their orders forever. That's blind obedience, not gratitude.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: With their days numbered, the Infected have no choice but to cling onto a belief or hope. It doesn't matter whether they have to sacrifice or become violent for it.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: But the same can't be said for us. So, we don't have to adopt the same belief as them and force ourselves to live in a place where we're made to feel fear and hate.
Some not-so-distant memories are coming back to me.
Before I can weave those memories into words, a commotion suddenly comes from outside the window.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: What's going on outside?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Seems like... a conflict has arisen during the evacuation process?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I'll go take a look.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Out of your responsibility as a Rhodes Island operator?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: No, because it's the right thing to do.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: (*shrugs*) I'll tag along.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: What's going on here?

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: Over there... In the forest...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Is there a Catastrophe cloud?

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: Sir, is the Catastrophe about to strike?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Don't panic. It's still pretty far away. I have a portable reader with me; just give me a moment...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: It's coming sooner than expected, which is in six to twelve hours. It's still a storm.

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: Th-Then, what should we...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Evacuate immediately. Bring only essential items with you, as your safety is your top priority. Have you contacted the caravan? Can you reach them now?

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: No response from the caravan, but everyone here has a burdenbeast cart.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Forget the caravan and use your carts to evacuate the area first.

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: Yes! Thank you so much, sir!

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: GreyThroat, can you contact Rhodes Island?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...No problem. I've already sent over a text.

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: Uwaah... Mom... Dad...

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Hold on, what's that child doing crying in the middle of town with not even an adult around?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: What's wrong, kiddo? Why are you crying?

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: Waaaah... uwaaah...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Calm down, alright? Where are your parents?

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: Uwh... Mom and Dad... They're... they're....

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: I'm too scared to go back... Waaaah...

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Excuse me, do you know what's going on with this child?

steps.name: Nervous Townsperson
steps.text: ...Isn't that one of those Infected kids from the woods? What're they doing here?

steps.name: Nervous Townsperson
steps.text: Alas, the Catastrophe cloud is coming soon, yet their parents don't even take care of them.
As soon as we hear the kid is an Infected, Ian and I step backward at the same time.
The child starts crying even louder.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: The woods? What's that supposed to mean?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: The Infected here are driven out to the nearby woods. That's a relatively merciful way to handle them.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: The people inside those woods are...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I already sent someone over to notify them.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: People will naturally take action during times like these. They can see the Catastrophe clouds too, so they're not going to stick around, even without a warning.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: But they have no idea it could strike so soon. If they're delayed by a few hours...
I step forward and approach the terrified child again.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Hey, buddy... What are your parents doing right now?

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: Mom's bedridden... and Dad's outside finding herbs for her... Waaah...

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Do they have communicators with them?

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: Communi... caters?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Something like this. It rings, and you can use it to talk to people nearby.

steps.name: Terrified Child
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Sir!

steps.name: Infected Townsperson
steps.text: What is it? I'm busy!

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: About this child's parents...

steps.name: Infected Townsperson
steps.text: None of my business!

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: We still have six to twelve hours before the Catastrophe strikes! This child's mother is bedridden and the father is out searching for herbs. Would you mind helping me notify them?

steps.name: Infected Townsperson
steps.text: You first said we had three to five days, but now it's become less than half a day. How can I be sure the Catastrophe won't come the moment I head to the woods?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...Ian, we need to notify the Infected left in the woods.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: The nearby Originium is already in the middle of activation. The closer you get to the eye of the Catastrophe, the more likely you'll be exposed to Active Originium dust.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Letting a healthy person walk toward a Catastrophe without any inhibitors and proper protective gear is tantamount to murder.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Besides... they're just some Infected, right?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Ian, you...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: We're exactly the same.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Hello? Blaze, you busy?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: That's right. I'm in the northern town. There's a group of Infected in the woods here who has no idea when the Catastrophe is going to strike. I need inhibitors and protective equipment, ASAP.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...What? Do you need to get the engine guy drunk?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Up to you, as long as it doesn't cause any delays. Over.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You don't think Blaze is going to show up?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: You've been dealing with the Rhodes Island folks way longer than I have.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Indeed, some of the Infected do have a virtuous character, but only because they've always been that way.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: However, the Infected are generally a group of dying people.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: What lies at the core of their souls is despair. In order to survive, they'll become more violent, depraved, and unpredictable.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: That's why... you chose to step away and stop dealing with them.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: That's right. I chose to step away.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I can accomplish a lot without dealing with them.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I can still save a lot of lives from Catastrophes and prevent healthy people from becoming Infected. That's the choice I've made.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: 'It's all about saving more lives'?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: So, you're no stranger to our motto. Heard it in Wolumonde?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Unfortunately, I'm not qualified to be a Contingency Contract Messenger yet.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Thank goodness for that.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I don't agree with everything they do, but...

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: They're just trying to save more lives.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: What about the lives of the Infected?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: They, too, count as lives, but... their lives have been corrupted, so they are shorter and more dangerous. We must prioritize healthy people before them.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You'd better not let Blaze hear you say that... No, don't you say that in front of me ever again.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: You mentioned 'blind obedience' just now.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Not too long ago, someone told me the same thing.

steps.name: Faust
steps.text: If you only follow orders, if you rely on everyone else to tell you what to do, that can only end poorly.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: How so?

steps.name: Faust
steps.text: Most of the sheep who blindly take orders aren't actually dependent on anyone. They just haven't started thinking for themselves...

steps.name: Faust
steps.text: And those who have no direction in life, they're just empty machines looking for a sense of accomplishment, and meaning.

steps.name: Faust
steps.text: You activate, and perform your function, you input a goal, you achieve your goal, until you consume everything around you, and you consume those you serve.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I'm not like that.

steps.name: Faust
steps.text: You're inexperienced.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: He was also an Infected, Ian. He wasn't even part of Rhodes Island, but an enemy.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I'm not sure if I was blindly following orders back then, but now... I know exactly what I'm doing.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I've spent years on Rhodes Island, groping around in the dark. No matter what, that's where my friends and the people important to me are. And among them are both ordinary people and Infected people.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Ian, aren't you also running away from the Infected?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: When we found out that child was infected, and when Blaze first walked into the room... you looked even more scared than I was.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Maybe we were the same at some point, but not anymore.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: At the very least, I no longer feel fear and hatred toward other people.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm here!

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: The inhibitors and protective gear.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Got 'em all here. Does this gentleman here need anything?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: No need. He's not going in.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I see. Anything else you'd like to say to him?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Ian, if I came out of these woods infected... would you still want me to be your bodyguard?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: This is no laughing matter. You can't conceal your fear as your voice is trembling.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: That's right. I'm scared to death, but I'll never let it get the better of me.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Answer my question, Ian.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: The answer is no. If you got infected, I wouldn't want you as my bodyguard.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: I know this sounds harsh, but... nothing will change my attitude toward the Infected.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Even if you've never had a proper conversation with an Infected?

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: ...That's right.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Alright. I guess there's nothing more to say.

steps.name: Catastrophe Messenger
steps.text: Rhodes Island... has taught you well.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I'll take that as a compliment.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wait, GreyThroat! Hold on!

a.text: The child's parents lived on the outskirts of the forest. Upon hearing our warning, the haggard man carried his wife on his back and ran out of the woods.
Meanwhile, their child was still sitting in the town square, clutching their knees to their chest.
In the end, Blaze and I spent two hours spreading the news of the Catastrophe to every corner of the woods that could possibly provide shelter.
Four hours after Rhodes Island set sail, the Catastrophe struck the empty town and the woods.
By then, I was dozing off in the dorms, having completed the routine disinfection and check-up.
In the dream, it was the day my mother first brought me to Rhodes Island. She took me, a young child, to the huge landship to meet one person after another.

Amiya had an amicable vibe that drew people to her. I willingly opened my heart to her even though she was an Infected. As for Dr. Kal'tsit, I didn't see her often, but every decision she made was convincing.
There's a big Feline who only knows how to shed blood everywhere. The two of us just went rampaging through some woods I'd never seen before.
There was Phidia who didn't talk much and whom I only met briefly. Also, there was a white Cautus, whose icy aura dissuaded me from approaching.
I knew that my mother was on the verge of a mental breakdown, perhaps already past the breaking point... In any case, she was not completely lucid.
But still, she entrusted me to Rhodes Island.
Countless times, I've wondered how I would have turned out if she had left me somewhere else, probably a place without the Infected.
However, right now, as I gaze into those indistinct eyes, I see a light in them that always flickers but has never gone out.
